title: 1899-23 Hartland Superior School, lower Main Street
description: James H. Grey became the first teacher at Hartland after 1871. On November 1, 1885, the school earned Superior status. Although this picture is not of the first school in the area, the Hartland Superior School was a modern school for its time, constructed in 1899 for $4,000 and featuring four rooms. Upstairs, the south side housed high school grades eight to eleven, while the north side contained a gramophone and equipment for scientific experiments. A fire exit was not installed until 1918. Both floors had wide halls, and a sink with a water tap was located at the foot of the south stairs on the main floor. Downstairs, the two rooms off the main hall included Grades 1–3 on the left and Grades 4–7 on the right (south). A tool room for garden equipment, wheelbarrows, and bicycles occupied the southwest corner. As the student population grew, the school expanded: in 1921–22, the science lab was relocated to the attic, and both the former lab and tool room were converted into classrooms. The gymnasium was also situated in the attic. There were no indoor toilets; the girls’ outhouse was on the southeast side, and the boys’ was on the northeast corner. The school was located on the east side of Main Street, where Tracey Demerchant's home now stands in 2026.
